title: Set Bits for Every Number up to n
statement:
You get a non-negative integer n. Return an array counts of length n + 1, where counts[i] is the number of 1 bits in the binary form of i, for every i from 0 to n inclusive.

Counting each number separately is O(n log n). Aim for O(n): one constant-time step per entry.

examples.why: 0, 1, 10, 11, 100, 101, 110 in binary. Seven entries, since 0 counts too.
Still one entry, for 0 itself. An empty array is wrong.
The count does not grow steadily: 7 = 111 has three bits, then 8 = 1000 drops back to one.

hints: Counting each number on its own works. Can the answer for i reuse an answer you already have?
Shifting i right by one drops its last bit. How does the count of i >> 1 relate to the count of i?
counts[i] = counts[i >> 1] + (i & 1). The smaller number is always computed already.

explain.intuition:
Write i in binary and chop off the last digit. What remains is i >> 1, a smaller number, so its count is already in the array. The chopped digit is i & 1. So counts[i] = counts[i >> 1] + (i & 1). For example, 13 = 1101: drop the last bit to get 110 = 6, which has 2 bits, and add the dropped 1 to get 3.

This is dynamic programming where every entry depends on one earlier entry, like a memo cache that is filled in order so every lookup hits. A second recurrence works the same way: i & (i − 1) is i without its lowest 1 bit, so counts[i] = counts[i & (i − 1)] + 1.
steps: Create counts with n + 1 zeros. counts[0] = 0 is the base case.
pitfalls: Returning n entries instead of n + 1. The range includes both 0 and n.
Using counts[i − 1] + 1. It holds for even i only. Going from 7 to 8 the count drops from 3 to 1.
Writing counts[i >> 1] + i & 1 without parentheses. + binds tighter than &, so it computes (counts[i >> 1] + i) & 1.

complexity.space: O(n) for the output, O(1) extra

solutions.title: Count each number separately
solutions.idea: For each i, clear its lowest set bit until it is 0 and count the steps.

solutions.title: Reuse the count of i >> 1
solutions.idea: Dropping the last bit gives a smaller number that is already counted. Add back the dropped bit.

solutions.title: Reuse the count of i without its lowest bit
solutions.idea: i & (i − 1) removes exactly one 1 bit, and it is smaller than i. So add 1 to its count.

followups: Write a third recurrence based on the highest power of two that is ≤ i. What do you need to track as i grows?
Only the total number of set bits across 0..n is needed, and n can be 10¹⁸. How do you count per bit position without building the array?
